lines.text: At Iconium, Paul and Barnabas spoke in the synagogue, and a great number of Jews and Greeks believed.
When they learned of the plot to stone them, Paul and Barnabas fled to Lystra and Tarsus and kept preaching.
In Lystra, Paul told a man lame from birth to stand, and the crowd called Barnabas Zeus and Paul Hermes.
Some Jews won over the crowds and stoned Paul in Lystra, and next day he left for Perga.
They appointed elders in each church, sailed from Attalia to Antioch, and reported that God opened faith's door to Gentiles.
